## Detailed entries

### Colfax County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** Reported adopted 'late last month' (late August 2026) per CPR.org's September 3, 2026 article; a public hearing on the proposed ordinance was held August 11, 2026 and the county's own public notice states the Board of Commissioners could consider adoption at its August 25, 2026 meeting.
- **Date field:** `2026-08-25` (unverified)
- **Duration:** One year from the effective date; the retained unsigned ordinance provides effectiveness 30 days after clerk recordation and automatic repeal one year later. Executed text and recordation date remain to be verified.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `nm-colfax-county-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Ordinance No. 2026-02 (Colfax County), 'An Ordinance for a Data Center Moratorium,' prohibiting the establishment or expansion of any data center in unincorporated areas of the county and putting municipalities within the county on notice that the county opposes data centers in incorporated areas as well; public hearing held August 11, 2026 per the county's official notice, adoption considered at the August 25, 2026 commission meeting.
- **What prompted it:** Concern over water use during a severe/extreme drought affecting the county, plus concerns about energy use, heat, and noise; came after the City of Raton's since-expired memorandum of understanding with a data-center developer (Atterix LLC) drew controversy.
- **Affected projects:** None sited in unincorporated Colfax County; the City of Raton separately had a since-expired memorandum of understanding with Atterix LLC to consider a data center at a former K-Mart site, but that is a municipal, not county, matter and is unaffected by this county ordinance.
- **Status notes:** CPR reported on September 3, 2026 that commissioners unanimously adopted a one-year moratorium late in August on data centers in unincorporated Colfax County. The retained county text is unsigned and provides effectiveness 30 days after recordation; the exact adoption date, recordation and later legal force have not been established. Municipalities retain authority over their own land use. [VERIFY: executed ordinance, recordation, operative interval and subsequent action.]
- **Outcome:** Colfax County Commission unanimously adopted a one-year moratorium on new or expanded data centers in unincorporated county territory.

### HB 27 (2026), Technology Jobs R&D Tax Credit Expansion

- **Policy ID:** `nm-hb-27-2026-technology-jobs-r-d-tax-credit-expansion`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Meredith A. Dixon, Sen. Michael Padilla, Rep. Joshua N. Hernandez, Rep. Linda Serrato, Sen. Nicole Tobiassen; Mixed (Dixon, Padilla, Serrato are D; Hernandez and Tobiassen are R; bipartisan cosponsorship per NM Legislature member rosters)
- **Status:** Died in House Taxation and Revenue Committee (Action Postponed Indefinitely) after House Commerce and Economic Development Committee reported Do Not Pass on the original bill but Do Pass on a committee substitute on 2026-01-29; not enacted before 2026 sine die (2026-02-19)
- **Provisions:** The HCEDC substitute proposed expanding the technology jobs and research and development tax credit, including treatment of certain industrial revenue bond property, while excluding data centers from the definition of qualified facility. It died in committee.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; unknown
- **Legal effect:** failed

- **End condition and limitations:** —

### SB 235 (2026), Microgrid Oversight Act

- **Policy ID:** `nm-sb-235-2026-microgrid-oversight-act`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Jeff Steinborn, Sen. Antoinette Sedillo Lopez, Rep. Joanne J. Ferrary, Rep. Patricia Roybal Caballero; D (all four are NM Democrats)
- **Status:** Senate Conservation Committee substitute recommended; Senate Tax, Business and Transportation Committee recommended Do Pass (report dated 2026-02-12, recorded 2026-02-13), not a second substitute. Passed Senate 22-20 on 2026-02-14; sent to House Judiciary Committee 2026-02-15; Action Postponed Indefinitely there; not enacted before 2026 sine die (2026-02-19).
- **Provisions:** The Senate Conservation Committee substitute proposed oversight of qualifying microgrids, renewable portfolio requirements and annual reporting, alongside limits on public utility rate increases for microgrid infrastructure. A February14 Senate floor amendment proposed county/population-based exemptions from the renewable portfolio standard, but the official bill history lists that amendment under Not Adopted; those exemptions were not adopted through that amendment. The bill failed in House committee. The fiscal report discusses data-center energy needs using agency comments on similar legislation; this does not establish that a particular data center qualifies.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://www.nmlegis.gov/Legislation/Legislation?Chamber=S&LegType=B&LegNo=235&year=26>)
